clinical.disclaimer: Screening aid only. Results are produced by automated image analysis and are not a medical diagnosis, and the tool can miss disease. It has not been clinically validated. Always have a qualified eye-care professional review the findings before making any treatment decision.

No_DR.title: Overall Assessment: Stage 0 – No DR detected

clinical.idleNote: Upload fundus images for both eyes and run the AI assessment to see the screening result.

none.title: No Assessment Yet
none.sub: Upload both fundus images on the dashboard and run the AI assessment. Nothing on this page should be read as a result until then.

noReferral.title: No Referral Flagged
noReferral.sub: The screening model did not flag diabetic retinopathy in either eye. This does not rule out disease: the tool can miss it. Continue regular eye screening as advised by your eye-care professional.

followUp.title: Follow-up Recommended
followUp.sub: The screening model detected mild changes. Follow-up with an eye-care professional is recommended; ask them how often you should be screened.

referral.title: Specialist Review Recommended
referral.sub: The screening model flagged possible diabetic retinopathy in at least one eye. Review by an eye-care professional is recommended; this result cannot be acted on automatically.

clinical.basisScore: Basis: referral score compared with a {{threshold}} threshold
clinical.basisScoreSite: Basis: referral score compared with a {{threshold}} threshold set by this site
clinical.confidenceNote: Lower confidence means the grade is less likely to be right. In testing, the referral decision was wrong in about 1% of high-confidence results and about 15% of the rest.
clinical.stageNote: The referral decision is the more reliable output. On held-out test images it found about 95% of referable cases, while the exact stage matched the reference grade about 78% of the time. Results depend on the camera and population: on a second public dataset it flagged many more eyes that had no disease (see validation/REPORT.md).
clinical.referralChipHint: The most likely stage is lower, but the screening model's referral threshold was reached
clinical.heatmapNote: Shows the regions that raised this eye's referral score, on a coarse grid. A rough guide, not a lesion detection: warm colours do not by themselves mean disease, and disease can be present outside them.
clinical.heatmapBelow: This eye's referral score is below the threshold, so it was not flagged. The map shows where the score was relatively highest, not a finding.
clinical.heatmapEmpty: No region raised this eye's referral score, so nothing is highlighted. That does not rule out disease.
clinical.lesionNote: Coloured areas are possible lesions for a clinician to check, not findings. In testing, the lesion model marked something in about 1 in 3 eyes that had no retinopathy, and it misses some lesions.
clinical.lesionNoneNote: The lesion model marked nothing in this photograph. That does not rule out disease.
clinical.pdfPrivacy: The PDF prints the patient's name and date of birth from their profile. To create it, the photographs are sent to the server again; the server does not keep the photographs or the report file.
clinical.pdfNeedsAssessment: Run the AI assessment first; the PDF report is made from its result.
clinical.pdfNeedsPhotos: The photographs are no longer in this session. Upload them and run the assessment again to make a PDF report.
clinical.englishOnly: This result text is shown in English only, because no checked-in-advance sentence exists for it in this language.
